raised.claim: Measuring token length after an ASCII-only fold drops genuine multi-character words from the query.
raised.why_it_breaks: With brewery `Pinta` and beer name `Øl`, `foldToken('Øl')` is `l` because `Ø` survives NFD but is removed by the ASCII filter. The query changes from `Pinta Øl` to `Pinta`, losing the entire beer name even though it has two letters. The same length check also affects brewery tokens.

raised.claim: When the new filter removes every token, the fallback sends the rejected one-character name and discards the brewery.
raised.why_it_breaks: With brewery `Q Brewery` and beer name `7`, the old result is `Q 7`. The new checks reject both `Q` and `7`, but the fallback returns `7` alone. This still sends the kind of query the PR identifies as yielding zero hits and loses the brewery in the process.

raised.claim: The new length check can miss one-character search terms embedded in punctuation-separated names.
raised.why_it_breaks: With beer name `Rock-n-Roll`, the loop sees one token whose fold is `rocknroll`, then sends the original `Rock-n-Roll` unchanged. If Algolia splits the hyphens into term boundaries, it still receives the standalone `n`, so the zero-hit failure remains for that spelling.
